clue.text: Dependant in the family was the soul of discretion

definitions.meaning: read literally: a mother who is kept, supported by the rest of the household
the idiom for saying nothing, in the past tense to match 'was'

explanation.surface: A relative living off the family who never breathed a word of its secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the idiom into its words, a mum who is kept; the second uses it whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is an idiom for staying silent, which is what the soul of discretion does.

clue.text: Light touch: knock is somewhat stronger, first of all

indicators.note: 'first of all' taken literally asks for the first letter of all the words before it

parts.note: the first letters of Knock, Is, Somewhat, Stronger. The same letters also run on unbroken across neighbouring clue words, a coincidence of the pieces sitting side by side; the setter gives no hidden-word signal.

explanation.surface: A boxing coach saying a tap is fine, but the first blow should land a bit harder.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Light touch' look like a heading for advice about knocking, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle brush of the lips against someone is about the lightest touch there is.

clue.text: Uranium breaking lump into twisted metal

indicators.note: twisted things are out of shape, so LUMP INTO is rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
LUMP INTO rearranged, with U going in after PL

explanation.surface: A uranium sample cracking a lump of scrap and leaving it as twisted metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The chemistry is apt: this element is made by bombarding uranium, and it is a radioactive metal like the one in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a radioactive metallic element, used in nuclear reactors and weapons.

clue.text: Life-savers — 'renc' 'octor'?

parts.note: the surface wants lifeguards or sweets; the setter means a body of people who save lives

explanation.walkthrough: There are no letters to build: the two stumps picture the charity's French name, doctors without borders, by showing French and doctor without their edges.
explanation.definitionFit: The international medical charity works in war and disaster zones, saving lives.

clue.text: Police arresting Indian queen after climbing tall spire

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads upwards

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen or princess

explanation.surface: Officers seizing an Indian queen who has shinned up a tall spire.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen really is climbing in the surface, which is why her title reads upwards; the Met is London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made, is a tall spire.

clue.text: Progressive learner yours truly scolded

explanation.surface: A pupil complaining that the forward-thinking learner, meaning the speaker, got told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progressive learner' reads as one phrase about a pupil, but 'Progressive' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone free of conventional attitudes holds progressive views.

clue.text: Cross, when nail and contents of boot found in spoon!

explanation.surface: An exclamation at finding a nail and a boot's contents in a spoon.

clue.text: Board prepared to gather intelligence?

explanation.surface: Meals made ready to help you get smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Board means meals, as in bed and board, so the whole clue also reads straight: fare prepared to build intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for food thought to be good for the mind, which is board meant to feed intelligence.

clue.text: Cowboy for example in condition?

the legal sense: an extra clause or proviso added to an agreement

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cowboy is in good shape.

explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy is one who rides, and a rider to a contract is a condition tacked onto it.

clue.text: Inflammation, it's seen after time on shelf

clue.text: Dim case in office

an ark is a chest or box

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to make or grow less bright.

clue.text: Goddess, something of an observer?

definitions.meaning: the Greek goddess of the rainbow and messenger of the gods

explanation.surface: A goddess described as a bit of a watcher.

clue.text: Protestation in bar?

a barrier of metal bars, as round a park

clue.text: Dodgy joint, sufferer's heading over mountain before a walk in the park

clue.text: Hey-ho, safer on the beach is it?

definitions.text: Hey-ho, safer on the beach is it?

parts.note: a resigned shrug at a small setback

parts.words: safer on the beach is it?
parts.note: a question that takes the consoling saying literally: dry land beats the open water

clue.text: Advisor perhaps yawning over the telephone

clue.text: Drug stuffed in a corset

clue.text: Undeniably strength drops boxing in leader in triathlon

clue.text: Something sharp picked up, scent grouse

clue.text: Third person accepting introduction from Ronnie Barker?

parts.note: after Adam and Eve, their son was the third person in the Bible

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so take the first letter of Ronnie

clue.text: Septic tanks in the end redesigned — something like that?

clue.text: In meticulous fashion, but not exactly

explanation.walkthrough: 'But not exactly' reads as a hedge on the definition, but 'but' and 'not exactly' each supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe doing something with complete care.

clue.text: Follower of power in rogue I suspect

parts.note: ROGUE I rearranged, with P going in

clue.text: Slur, bit of a bloomer?

clue.text: Concerned with meal when fed a fresh starter?

clue.text: Tired, straight up?

clue.text: With runs to bag, get that job done right

clue.text: Growing crystals, good try cutting surfaces on eighty

clue.text: Soul in dream, in actuality lifted

clue.text: Charge more to cover rent, finally — and relax!

clue.text: No more cheers, say

clue.text: Remain taken by giant of the Himalayas?

clue.text: Splashing out conversation uniting nations?

clue.text: While sad, all relics for us initially confined to box

first letters of All Relics For Us

clue.text: Damned red card — is one really sympathetic?
